name: Dabigatran
summary: The only oral direct thrombin inhibitor, with a specific reversal antibody (idarucizumab) and a twice-daily dosing schedule.
mechanism: Prodrug (dabigatran etexilate) converted by esterases to dabigatran, a reversible direct inhibitor of free and clot-bound thrombin.
pharmacodynamics: Reversible, dose-dependent prolongation of thrombin time and aPTT.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Esterase hydrolysis to active dabigatran; no CYP involvement; P-gp substrate

dosing.adult: Nonvalvular AF: 150 mg twice daily (110 mg twice daily in EU for age ≥80 years); VTE treatment: 150 mg twice daily after 5–10 days of parenteral anticoagulation
dosing.renalAdjustment: US: 75 mg twice daily if CrCl 15–30 mL/min; avoid if CrCl <15 mL/min; avoid strong P-gp inhibitors in renal impairment

safety.pregnancy: Avoid — no adequate data; bleeding risk
warnings: Dyspepsia and GI bleeding (capsule contains tartaric acid)
Store in original container (moisture degrades the drug)
safety.overdose: Idarucizumab for life-threatening bleeding; dialysis removes dabigatran

indications: Stroke prevention in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation
Treatment of DVT/PE and prevention of recurrence
VTE prophylaxis after hip or knee replacement
clinicalPearls: The only DOAC with a specific reversal antibody (idarucizumab).
GI intolerance is the most common reason for discontinuation among DOACs.
good: Patients needing oral anticoagulation with a fully reversible agent.
bad: Patients with GI sensitivity, severe renal impairment, or mechanical heart valves.
